title: Getting what you need from the between-run shop
target: How the shop between runs in R.E.P.O. decides what it offers, so money goes on what the run needs rather than on what happens to be on the shelf.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A crew that agrees on what is missing
Enough runs to know what you keep losing

steps.do: Know the shop aims for an amount of stock rather than stocking by accident.
steps.because: it aims for a number of items, with separate amounts for consumables, upgrades and health packs (itemSpawnTargetAmount, itemConsumablesAmount, itemUpgradesAmount, itemHealthPacksAmount)

steps.do: Check what kinds of thing it can offer at all.
steps.because: its offerings are split into ordinary items, consumables, upgrades and health packs (potentialItems, potentialItemConsumables, potentialItemUpgrades, potentialItemHealthPacks)

steps.do: Look for secret stock, which is kept separately.
steps.because: the shop keeps separate volumes and items for secret stock (secretItemVolumes, potentialSecretItems)

steps.do: Read the prices the game gives you.
steps.because: shop costs are shown by the game rather than inferred (ShopCostUI)

steps.do: Buy upgrades at their stand, where their information is.
steps.because: upgrades are bought at a stand and carry their own information (UpgradeStand, ItemUpgrade, UpgradeInfo)

steps.do: Get cosmetics from the machine rather than from the shelves.
steps.because: cosmetics come from a separate machine (CosmeticShopMachine, CosmeticShopMachineAnimator)

steps.do: Expect the shop to track what you have bought.
steps.because: the shop holds the volumes it can use and the items it may offer, and an item manager keeps what has been purchased (ShopManager, itemVolumes, potentialItems, ItemManager)

commonMistakes: Spending on consumables when the crew keeps dying rather than running out of things.
Ignoring the upgrade stand and buying loose items instead.
Assuming a shelf holds everything the shop can sell.
Forgetting that the shop's stock is aimed at amounts rather than guaranteed.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
